sections.h2: Why is Lakeville, Minnesota, different from other Twin Cities suburbs for sellers?
sections.html:
Lakeville is the largest city in Dakota County and the ninth most populous in Minnesota, with 79,270 residents in the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate. It sits about 20 miles south of both downtown Minneapolis and downtown St. Paul along Interstate 35, and it grew 14.1 percent between April 2020 and mid-2025. That pace is the fastest of the four cities in the Census comparison, so sellers here deal with a market that keeps adding new homes alongside resales.

The city covers about 36 square miles of land. J. J. Brackett platted the town site in 1855 on a lake he called Prairie Lake; it was renamed Lake Marion after Marion Savage built the Dan Patch rail line to serve his Antlers Amusement Park in 1910. Lakeville was incorporated as a city in 1967 and stayed mostly agricultural until the interstate and rising metro land costs pulled housing south. Large farms growing corn, soybeans and dairy cattle still operate.

A branch of the Vermillion River, which the state has designated a trout stream, crosses Lakeville, and North Creek, one of its tributaries, starts in the northern part of the city. Winters are cold: weather-station data for 2010 to 2020 show a mean January daily high of 22.6 degrees Fahrenheit and a low of 10.4.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show about Lakeville homes and households?
sections.html:
Lakeville has the highest home values and incomes of the four cities in the Census comparison. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $452,500 for 2020-2024, and 87.8 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, with 25,685 households averaging 2.89 people.

sections.h2: Do Lakeville rental and short-term rental rules affect a house sale?
sections.html:
Yes, if the house is currently rented or you are considering renting it first. Lakeville's council adopted a residential rental registration ordinance in September 2023 for long-term rentals, defined as 32 days or longer. Registration is mandatory, free, and one-time unless contact information or ownership changes, and the city does not require inspections. Owners of several rentals must file a form for each property.

Short-term rentals are allowed only with a Short-Term Rental Administrative Permit under Title 9, Chapter 10 of city code. Highlights from the city's list of requirements:

  • Listings must show the city permit number, maximum occupancy and maximum number of vehicles.
  • Overnight guests are capped at two adults per bedroom plus their dependent children.
  • Guest vehicles must park in the garage or on the driveway, and noise must be reduced between 10:00 PM and 7:00 AM.
  • Owners pay local lodging tax under Title 3, Chapter 17 of city code.

A buyer who wants to run a rental after closing will ask whether the property is registered, so file the registration if you still hold the house as a rental.

sections.h2: Which Lakeville school district am I in, and why does it matter?
sections.html:
Most Lakeville households are in Lakeville Area School District 194, which runs two high schools, Lakeville North and Lakeville South, each with close to 2,000 students, plus nine elementary schools and three middle schools (Century, McGuire and Kenwood). Parts of northern and eastern Lakeville fall under District 196 (Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan) or Farmington District 192.

Because the boundaries date from the farming era, two neighbors can be in different districts. Minnesota's open enrollment law also lets families choose a school outside their home district. When you write your listing, name the exact district for the address so buyers do not have to guess.

sections.h2: Which employers, roads and areas draw buyers to Lakeville?
sections.html:
Airlake Industrial Park covers about 1,500 acres and holds as many as 200 companies with an estimated 4,500 employees. It is served by Airlake Airport, a reliever airport run by the Metropolitan Airports Commission. Post Consumer Brands has kept its headquarters in the city since 2015. The Minneapolis air route traffic control center sits a few miles away in Farmington.

Interstate 35 is the main artery, and Cedar Avenue (Minnesota Highway 77) runs along the east side. The Census puts the average commute at 23.6 minutes. The Argonne area, a post-World War I settlement project now covered with suburban retail, still appears by that name on maps.

sections.h2: How do I close the Lakeville water account and record the deed?
sections.html:
Lakeville bills residential water quarterly and calculates sewer charges from winter-quarter water use. The city's Form Center has an online stop-service form for sellers and a start-service form for buyers, and you can pay bills through InvoiceCloud, by mail, or at City Hall at 20195 Holyoke Avenue. Call the Utility Division at 952-985-2700 with questions about the meter.

Dakota County Property Taxation and Records records Lakeville deeds at its Hastings office. State deed tax of 0.0033 on a sale at the city's $452,500 median value comes to about $1,493. The county auditor must confirm there are no delinquent taxes before the deed can be recorded (Minnesota Statutes 272.12), and Minnesota Statutes 513.55 requires you to give the buyer a written disclosure of material facts before signing a purchase agreement.

Dakota County's 2026 tax calendar lists May 15 and October 15 as the due dates for the two halves of real estate tax. Late payments carry a 2 percent penalty on homestead property and 4 percent on other property under state law.

faqs.q: How big is Lakeville compared with nearby cities?
faqs.a: Lakeville is the largest city in Dakota County, at 79,270 people in the 2025 Census estimate. Farmington next door has 25,425 and Inver Grove Heights has 36,873. Its size means a large pool of potential buyers and a lot of new construction competing with resales.

faqs.q: Do I need to register my Lakeville rental before selling it?
faqs.a: Lakeville requires registration of residential rentals of 32 days or longer, with no fee and no inspection. Register each property once, and update the city if ownership or contact information changes.

faqs.q: Can a buyer run a short-term rental in a Lakeville house?
faqs.a: Only with a Short-Term Rental Administrative Permit from the city, and the owner must follow the Title 9, Chapter 10 performance standards. Those include listing the permit number and limiting guests to two adults per bedroom.

faqs.q: How much deed tax will I see on a Lakeville sale?
faqs.a: State deed tax is 0.0033 of the net price above $3,000. On a $452,500 sale, that is about $1,493. Your title company will show the exact figure on the closing statement.

faqs.q: Who do I contact to stop Lakeville utilities when I sell?
faqs.a: Use the Finance forms on the city's Form Center to stop service, or contact the Utility Division at 952-985-2700. Bills are quarterly, so ask for a final read that matches your closing date.
